operations.note: CLASSIFICATION IMPURITY, ruled 2026-07-29. The baseline operation also stages body hardware and electronics. It is counted wholly to the neck, which overstates neck cost slightly and therefore biases against the make case. Decision 2 forbids splitting an accepted operation in this sprint.

operations.description: Neck blank preparation and CNC machining including fret slotting
operations.note: THE ONLY OPERATION IN THE ENTIRE NECK THAT CARRIES SETUP. Its 18 minutes are the whole batching opportunity, worth 8.62 per neck at infinite quantity. The 52 machine minutes are per part and do not nest away.

operations.description: Fretboard installation: glue over the truss rod, clamp, level and radius
operations.note: DRAFT ADDITION. No fretboard-installation operation exists anywhere in the accepted V2 estimate. CORRECTED 2026-07-29: this was first written as 22 touch minutes, which charged clamp time as operator labour. Spreading glue and setting clamps is about 10 minutes of touch; the 45 minutes the glue then needs is ELAPSED WAIT and costs nothing. Both figures are unmeasured.

operations.description: Fret preparation: install, level, crown, polish, dress ends
operations.note: 53% of all neck touch time and the dominant sensitivity variable. A fret press with batch jigs is the only credible route to reducing it, and it has nothing to do with the router.

operations.description: Nut work: fit blank, cut slots to height, shape and polish
Preliminary neck setup: truss rod tension and initial relief

operations.note: DRAFT ADDITION. Neck finishing is absent from the ENTIRE accepted product model, not merely the neck - every finish operation in the V2 baseline is body work. Its omission means the baseline neck was never production-ready, so any earlier comparison against a finished purchased neck was not like-for-like. CORRECTED 2026-07-29: first written as 32 touch minutes, which charged cure time as labour. Spraying and scuff-sanding is about 15 minutes of touch, the booth is occupied 20 at the governed 4.22/hr spray-booth rate, and the 240-minute cure is elapsed wait costing nothing. All three figures are unmeasured.

notes: This is the LIKE-FOR-LIKE comparison: quality-matched to a shop-machined neck, and the only purchase reference the make case should be judged against.
Landed cost is unknown. Domestic or import status is unstated, so neither freight nor duty is assumed.

buy_references.description: Budget finished neck, imported, probable composite fingerboard
notes: NOT A LIKE-FOR-LIKE SUBSTITUTE and must not be compared as one.
Owner assessment: the workmanship may not pass inspection at all, in which case it is not an option at any price.
The fingerboard is probably composite, against AAA ebony at 29.00 on the in-house spec it was being compared with.

EVERY LANDED-COST FIELD IS UNKNOWN. Freight, duty under HTS 9209 plus any Section 301 line which must be verified current, incoming inspection, corrective fretwork and reject rate all sit between 45.00 and a usable neck.
A modelled hidden-cost structure suggests these roughly double the catalog figure, but nothing in it is measured, which is why no value is recorded here.

Heel-to-pocket fit is the specific risk for a CNC shop: the neck pocket is repeatable to hundredths of a millimetre and an imported heel is not. That mismatch costs labour on every instrument, not once.

back_calculation.note: Anchors on a KNOWN retail price and solves backwards, rather than treating a catalog figure as a cost. The output is a bracket, not a point: the four channel routes are plausible industry structures and their spread is the honest width of the answer.

margin_provenance.note: EVERY MARGIN HERE IS A RULE OF THUMB, not an observation of this manufacturer or this retailer. They are stated as a spread precisely because no single one is defensible. A real dealer invoice would collapse the bracket and is the measurement worth getting.

sensitivity.note: A deterministic grid, not an optimiser. Machine minutes remain PER NECK: this sprint does not reinterpret them as a nested batch runtime without measured evidence.

provenance.note: Wood prices and purchase references are owner-supplied research. Every operation time other than the two draft additions is carried from the accepted V2 baseline at commit 1cd74f9 and is not re-derived here.

notes: BATCHING IS THE SMALLEST LEVER ON THE TABLE. Only OP-4100 carries setup, so the entire benefit is 8.62 per neck and it is fully realised by about quantity 10.
The two real levers are the fretboard price and the fretwork time, and neither has anything to do with the router that prompted this sprint.
The construction choice is worth 11.75 per neck in timber alone, which is more than everything batching can offer combined.
